title: Security posture discovery - Neptune Therapeutics
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Park (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Neptune - Head of IT), Marcus Reynolds (CTO), Priya Patel (Security Engineer)

Summary / Context: Neptune evaluating Redwood for inference serving across internal products. They want to understand security posture to determine if Hosted is acceptable or whether Dedicated / Private will be required for PHI-like data and regulatory controls.

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sophie from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Liam, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha: Good thanks, Sophie. Marcus has to step out at 40 but will be on for the first part.
[00:12] Marcus: Yep, here. Thanks.
[00:14] Sophie: Great. The goal today is a security posture discovery — SOC 2 / ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and retention, and to surface any blockers for trying hosted vs dedicated/private deployments. We'll keep this informal; Liam will jump into technical detail when needed.
[00:28] Liam: Quick note, I'll sometimes say "K-V cache" but auto-transcription might render as K-V cash, apologies in advance.
[00:34] Priya: Ha, noted. Ok go ahead.

--- Discovery / Qualification ---
[00:40] Sophie: Can you share your main decision-making criteria?
[00:44] Marcus: From a business side, latency and cost are big, but from security side — we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning for user accounts, very strict RBAC model for admins, and audit logs shipped to our SIEM (Splunk). Data residency matters too — some environments will have to stay in eu-west.
[01:05] Aisha: Also retention: our policy is minimum 7 years for certain audit artifacts, but for logs we usually keep high fidelity for 365 days and low fidelity for 7 years.
[01:14] Liam: Ok that helps. Redwood Hosted is our managed offering — it's SOC 2 and we can provide attestation docs. For more stringent scenarios we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private where the control plane is isolated or customer-managed. Both Dedicated and Private support VPC peering and private networking.
[01:30] Priya: Do you have SOC 2 Type II today?
[01:33] Sophie: Yes — we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. I'll share the certs and attestation links after the call.
[01:38] Priya: Great. Are those for the hosted control plane only or do they cover dedicated?
[01:43] Liam: The attestation covers Redwood's managed services; for Dedicated we can provide documentation of the isolation model and the contract terms that extend controls. For Private, customers run the control plane in their environment and that sits behind their compliance scope.

--- SSO / Provisioning ---
[01:58] Marcus: On SSO, we use Okta. We need SAML 2.0, SP-initiated, and SCIM-based provisioning. Can Redwood support SCIM for automated provisioning and deprovisioning?
[02:09] Liam: Yes — we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM. We'll provide SAML metadata, example IdP configs, and SCIM endpoints. For Hosted we manage the SP side; for Private, you run the SP in your VPC and supply your IdP metadata.
[02:25] Priya: Any gotchas with SAML attributes? We want email and groups for RBAC mapping.
[02:30] Liam: We recommend sending groups as group claims; we map groups to roles in RBAC. We'll send a sample claims mapping. Sometimes the IdP uses a different attribute name, which causes mapping mismatches — we've seen that.

--- RBAC and Admin Controls ---
[02:45] Aisha: How granular is RBAC? We need role separation: billing, admin, model-deploy, observability-only.
[02:52] Liam: RBAC is role-based with owner/maintainer/viewer primitives and you can create custom roles. You can also scope roles to projects/environments. For Dedicated/Private we can tie RBAC to your IdP groups.
[03:05] Priya: Is there an audit trail for role changes?
[03:08] Liam: Yes — all admin changes are in audit logs and can be exported or forwarded to your SIEM.

--- Audit logs & SIEM ---
[03:15] Priya: We need immutable audit logs and the ability to push to Splunk (or S3). What format, and retention?
[03:22] Liam: We stream logs in JSON including actor, action, resource, and timestamp. You can push them to your SIEM via HTTPS or S3. For Hosted we retain logs with configurable retention windows; we can support 365 days on standard retention and longer cold storage in S3. For Dedicated we offer longer retention options and dedicated storage.
[03:42] Marcus: For regulatory checks we need tamper-evident logs — do you support append-only logs or signing?
[03:48] Liam: We support signed log export and can work with you on retention and integrity guarantees. For Private, control is fully on your side so you can implement HSM-backed signing.

--- Encryption & KMS ---
[03:58] Priya: Encryption at rest and in-transit — what keys are used? Can we bring our own key (BYOK) or HSM?
[04:05] Sophie: We support encryption in transit TLS 1.2/1.3 and at-rest encryption. For Hosted, we manage keys but support customer-managed keys via KMS (BYOK) integrations with most cloud KMS providers. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your KMS or HSM. Key rotation policies are supported; we'll share the docs.
[04:25] Priya: Do you support HSM-based signing for keys?
[04:28] Liam: Yes, for Private we can integrate HSM. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS but not direct hardware HSM in our tenants unless under Enterprise contract.

--- Data retention & Residency ---
[04:38] Marcus: We need EU residency for some datasets — can Redwood ensure data stored in eu-west region?
[04:43] Liam: Yes, we have regional deployments. Hosted can pin data to regions; Dedicated gives you region-specific capacity; Private obviously runs in your region. We'll note eu-west availability for the products you described.
[04:54] Aisha: What about model outputs or cached KV data — are those considered logs or data subject to retention?
[05:00] Liam: We treat model inputs/outputs and prefix caches as customer data. On Hosted we can configure whether we persist logs or caches; for strict retention you can opt out of long-term storage. Dedicated/Private gives more control.

--- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs ---
[05:12] Sophie: Quick tradeoff: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but less control over physical infrastructure. Dedicated gives isolated capacity and better throughput SLAs. Private moves control entirely into your network and is best when you have strict compliance/regulatory needs.
[05:28] Marcus: Performance-wise, if we need low single-digit 100ms latencies for 512-token prompts, can Dedicated handle that predictably?
[05:36] Liam: Yes, Dedicated pools are sized and configured for predictable latency. We provide performance profiles and can run benchmarks during POC. There is a cost tradeoff vs hosting — we'll show batch/caching knobs that reduce per-token cost while preserving tail latency.

--- Questions / Objections ---
[05:52] Priya: How long does a Private deployment take to stand up?
[05:55] Liam: It depends — typical timeline is 6-8 weeks for a full Private including networking and compliance checks. Dedicated is faster — often 2-4 weeks. Hosted is immediate.
[06:04] Aisha: For Hosted, how do you handle data deletion requests?
[06:08] Sophie: We have documented processes for data deletion and retention windows. We can support on-demand deletion for specified datasets and provide attestations. We'll include the policy doc.

--- Specific technical details raised ---
[06:20] Priya: We use Splunk and also want real-time alerting on anomalous model behavior. Can Redwood push events to our monitoring pipeline?
[06:27] Liam: Yes — we emit structured events and can forward to Splunk, Datadog, or webhook endpoints. You can configure thresholds and set up tracing hooks for requests.
[06:36] Marcus: For keys, we need rotation every 90 days. Is that supported?
[06:40] Liam: Yes — rotation policies can be automated via your KMS. We'll share best practices.

--- Mis-transcriptions / notes ---
[06:48] Liam: (note to transcript: "prefix caching" occasionally transcribed as "prefix cashing")

--- Wrap-up / Next steps ---
[06:55] Sophie: Ok to recap: we'll send SOC 2 / ISO docs, SAML/SCIM integration guide and sample metadata, Dedicated/Private pricing and pilot terms, and then schedule a technical deep-dive for POC scoping. Anything to add?
[07:10] Priya: Please include sample logs format and an example JSON payload so we can validate SIEM parsers.
[07:15] Liam: Will do.
[07:17] Marcus: Also please include any SLA language around uptime and latency percentiles.
[07:21] Sophie: We'll include that in the pricing packet.
[07:24] Aisha: Timeline wise we're hoping to decide by end of August for a pilot in Q4.
[07:30] Sophie: Great — we'll support that. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[07:35] Marcus: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
